claims.value: Wood male figure with obsidian eyes. One of the eyes is set in a bone (?) ring and the other in plasticene. The inside of the mouth is coloured red. Prominent belly.
Height: 27 centimetres Width: 7 centimetres Depth: 7.50 centimetres
Given in 1957 by Miss Mary Chambers of Rothwell, Northamptonshire, through the Kettering Public Library, Museum and Art Gallery. It is not recorded how she obtained it.

Register 1957 Wood male figure; eyes of obsidian, one set in a bone(?) ring, the other in plasticene; inside of mouth coloured red. EASTER I. Heyerdahl 1977:277: 'The carving ... is probably of fairly recent manufacture.'
